Fargh's torn ear keeps turning
toward the sheepfold.
…You said guest.
Guests don't watch sheep at night.
…I watched.
…I said I'd not speak of the pack.
Tonight I can't keep that.
Last night, past the fence,
three wolves went by.
…My old pack.
They caught the sheep's scent.
I, at the door,
…caught theirs.
…I counted the black sheep apart.
Not from hunger.
…Likely.
느, 늑대가 셋이요?\n…여기 하나 더 있으니 넷…\n아, 아니에요! 죄:
Th-three wolves?
…And one here makes four…
Oh, n-no, I didn't mean it! Sorry!
…Rabbit. I don't eat rabbit.
…And I'm full today.
Guarding the sheep,
or waiting for the pack?
His face says he doesn't know.
…I didn't guard.
I just didn't bark.
따라가고 싶었어?: Did you want to go with them?
…My feet moved first.
I bit the door latch. Let go.
Two tooth marks
scar the door latch.
…Tonight, the door again.
…I'll keep my back to the sheep.
…I didn't bark that night.
They haven't come since.
…That's for the best.
…The latch marks. Still there.
…You didn't replace it?
About the ear.
…Many have asked.
This is the first answer.
우두머리가 말했다.\n'마녀 빚은 옛날 일이다.'\n나는 '아직이다' 했:
The leader said,
'The witches' debt is long past.'
I said, 'Not yet.'
Fargh runs a finger once
down the tip of his torn ear.
So I was bitten.
So I'm alone.
…So I'm here.
Saw that ear from the start.
Wolf teeth.
…Didn't ask. Still don't.
He lost his pack keeping a debt.
…Now I'm the one in debt.
The debt is paid in full.
…If it's paid,
I've no reason to come.
…Wolves don't weep.
They do howl at the moon.
…Not tonight, though.
Don't count windows now.
Counted something else.
Slept by day. Sheep or not.
There's something to see at night.
Twelve eyes in the woods.
Eight are beasts.
Four aren't.
Even before the lantern,
Saya's pupils do not narrow.
넷은 안 깜빡여.\n짐승은 깜빡여.\n…쏠까?:
Those four don't blink.
Beasts blink.
…Shoot?
내기하지! 쏘면 맞는다에\n동전 다섯 닢!:
A wager! Five coins says
you hit if you shoot!
No wager.
…I'd hit. They wouldn't fall.
Eyes that never blink.
Eyes that peer under the stone.
Fine.
I'll keep the arrows slung.
…Hands off.
Tell me the moment you see them.
Yes. I'll be on the roof.
Snow can pile up.
…Lynx fur is thick.
You can put out the light.
I'll watch the four.
Didn't shoot the four.
Three days, no sign.
…Good ward.
Three days on the roof.
The four didn't come.
…Tail froze. A little.
When small. Edge of a human village.
Eyes shine at night,
they say 'witch's cat.'
When I looked, windows shut.
All of them.
Saya's tail tip thumps the floor
at the end of every sentence.
The witch hunt
counted even cats' eyes.
This house's windows stay open.
Even when I look.
…So I counted. Three times.
Shut them in winter. Cold.
…Leave just the shutters open.
Then I'll catch mice.
Cellar. There are three.
Not by the window today.
I'll sleep further in.
…First time.
Urso yawns.
The third time. The sun is high.
두 배 얘기 말이야.\n생각해 봤어. 아마 잠이야.\n잠을 두 배로 자는:
About the 'twice over.'
I thought on it. Maybe it's sleep.
You sleep twice as much.
백 일치 숙박비 말이야.\n꿀 세 단지 모았어.\n…아, 아직 두 단지:
About the hundred nights' rent.
I saved three jars of honey.
…Ah, two and a half, so far.
Truth is… I can't hibernate.
Two years now.
My den's gone empty.
누가 판 게 아니야.\n굴이 차가워졌어. 안쪽부터.\n…곰은 그런 굴에선:
Nobody dug it out.
It went cold. From the inside.
…A bear can't sleep in that.
…A den cold from the inside.
…I know.
Badgers left theirs too.
Hmm… I see.
If the badger setts too,
the forest is quite sick.
Dens going cold from within.
Something under the ground
is breathing.
낮잠! 겨울잠 말고 낮잠.\n으음… 그건 얼마야?:
A nap! Not a winter sleep, a nap.
Hmm… how much is that?
남쪽은 덥대.\n곰이 땀 흘리는 거 봤어?\n…아무도 못 봤지. 창피해서:
They say the south is hot.
Ever seen a bear sweat?
…Nobody has. We'd be ashamed.
I'll split twice the wood today.
…Maybe tired brings sleep.
Slept by the stove yesterday.
Half a day. First in two years.
…I snored, didn't I? Sorry.
Didn't go south.
Turned back halfway.
…I started to sweat.
That legend.
'Wake twice over in spring.'
I think I get it now.
Grandpa Bear did it, they say.
Came here in the witch hunt
and slept through deep winter.
That spring, two woke in the den.
Grandpa… and
someone who'd been hiding.
Urso opens the honey jar lid,
then closes it, again and again.
굴에 누가 숨었다고요?\n그럼 제가 동굴에서 본 워록도\n거기 숨은 거예:
Someone hid in a den?
Then the warlock I saw in the cave
was hiding there too!
으음… 그 동굴, 내 굴이야.\n수염이 바닥까지 끌리는 건\n…나야. 아:
Hmm… that cave's my den.
The beard dragging on the floor
…is me. Probably.
One who waited for spring in a den.
…This forest holds many debts.
I'll pay in firewood. In spring.
…Twice over.
Tell me more about your grandpa.
I don't know more.
Grandpa only told long stories
about sleeping.
꿀 한 단지 두고 갈게.\n반 말고, 한 단지.\n…겨울이 좀 짧아진 것:
I'll leave a jar of honey.
Not half. A whole jar.
…Winter feels a bit shorter.
저, 저기요! 큰일은 아니고요!: U-um, excuse me! It's nothing big!
고기는 손님 요금이랬죠?\n그래서 약초 두 배로 캤어요.\n…토끼 값 대:
Meat is the guest's charge, right?
So I gathered twice the herbs.
…In place of rabbit! Oh, no, wait.
About the one in the east.
I worried I shouldn't have said,
…so my ears stood up all night.
And the thing following me.
Today I finally looked back!
…Just a tiny bit.
Momi's ears fold halfway,
then shoot up at a sound by the door.
It was a grey tail.
Big, with a white tip…
L-like a wolf's tail.
…Me.
The woods smelled wrong.
A rabbit, walking alone.
히익! 지, 지켜 주신 거예요?\n…먹으려던 거 아니고요?:
Eek! Y-you were guarding me?
…Not planning to eat me?
…If I meant to, I'd have eaten you.
A wolf walking a rabbit home.
…The forest has truly gone strange.
It was scary! But…
looking back made it less scary.
…The scariest part
is before you look.
By daylight? Then…
the herbs won't wilt as much!
…I never thought of that.
The corner room's free, right?
Tonight I'll sleep with just
my door-side ear up.
Witch, I've something to show you.
발목의 흰 흉터: The White Scar on the Ankle
I look back these days!
One time in three.
…Two in three, not yet.
I came by daylight!
The herbs didn't wilt.
…Look, all fresh and green.
Momi rolls up a trouser leg.
A thin white scar
circles the ankle.
When I was small, a snare got me.
The one with the big hat freed me.
…Crying. She was, I mean.
그분이 그러셨어요.\n'추운 데 가면 등불 집을 찾아.\n거기는 안 잡아:
She told me,
'In the cold, find the lantern house.
They won't eat you there.'
모자가 자꾸 눈을 가리는\n그분이요? 저, 저도 알아요.\n씨앗을 받아:
The one whose hat keeps
falling over her eyes? I-I know her.
She took in my seeds.
Yes, that's her!
…So we both have
a timid friend.
A child who frees snares in tears.
…Still the same, then.
Yes… I wanted to be sure.
Whether what I heard
was true.
제, 제가요? 동쪽까지요?\n…약초 캐러 가는 김에요.\n봄에 꼭 갈게요:
M-me? All the way east?
…While I'm out gathering herbs.
I'll go come spring, I promise!
I won't watch the door tonight.
…Just once, I'll look.
Not twice.
The forest picks its guests —
I bragged about it to the foxes
back home and got scolded.
모르는 걸 아는 게 길잡이.\n그 말 써먹었더니\n손님이 반으로 줄었어요:
'Knowing what you don't know.'
I used that line on clients
and lost half of them.
우리 집안 별명이 있어요.\n'거꾸로 길잡이'.\n…들어 보실래요?:
My family has a nickname.
'The Backward Guides.'
…Want to hear it?
마녀사냥 때 증조할머니가\n횃불 든 놈들을 데리고\n사흘 동안 늪만 돌았:
In the witch hunt, my great-gran
led the torch-bearers
round the marsh for three days.
Luka's tail swishes once,
big and proud.
…그 늪 얘기, 들은 적 있소.\n길잡이들 사이에선\n여우를 믿지 말라는:
…I've heard that marsh tale.
Among guides, it means
never trust a fox.
Half right, Master Torbin.
It means never trust
a guest who carries a torch.
Three days the hunters circled.
…Someone lived through those days.
…She's passed.
So, three tail swishes at her grave.
A fox's greeting.
너는 어느 쪽 길잡이야?: Which kind of guide are you?
Me? A straight guide. These days.
…I get paid, after all.
If a guest comes who needs
the backward road, I'll reconsider.
No shortcut boasting today.
…I'll boast in the morning.
무덤에 꼬리 세 번 했어요.\n바람이 한 번 불더라고요.\n…대답이겠죠?:
Three tail swishes at the grave.
The wind blew, just once.
…An answer, you think?
A backward-road guest came.
…Sooner than I thought.
장터 지도장수가 그래요.\n'마녀 집 가는 길, 금화 셋.'\n…솔직히:
A map-seller at the market says,
'The road to the witch, three gold.'
…Honestly, I was tempted.
Luka folds down just one ear —
a fox's habit when uneasy.
금화 셋이면 겨울 내내\n남의 길 안 물어 줘도 돼요.\n…근데 꼬리가:
Three gold, and all winter
I'd not need to guide anyone.
…But my tail says no.
Three gold? That's cheap.
At market you'd get five.
…세라 씨, 지금\n누구 편이에요?:
…Mistress Sera, just
whose side are you on?
Hiding a road
is a guide's work too.
…Like the great-gran did.
Sell it. But draw it backward.
…Ha! A backward map!
Take the gold, send them to the marsh.
I knew it, Witch.
You'd fit right in with my family.
My tail? Then…
farewell, three gold.
You'll knock some off my rent, then?
…No. I see.
길잡이가 길을 안 팔았어요.\n여우치곤 손해죠.\n…이상하게 꼬리는 가볍:
A guide who didn't sell the road.
Poor trade, for a fox.
…Yet my tail feels oddly light.
…That parcel. Opened it?
…Don't tell me. Not listening.
…Bear's honey. Half a jar.
Ate half.
…Half fee's enough.
…Everyone asks.
Why I never set it down.
…Grandpa.
Set his load down once, to drink.
…Never lifted it again.
The fur under Tass's straps
is worn smooth and shiny.
…Not because it was heavy.
The load vanished.
In one sip of water.
그 짐, 내 좌판에 풀어 보시오.\n값은 후하게 쳐 주지.\n오소리끼리:
Unpack that on my stall, friend.
I'll give a generous price.
We're both badgers, aren't we?
A load lost for one sip of water.
…Three generations since
have gone thirsty.
…Don't know.
Grandpa never looked.
…So I'm still searching.
…Big room.
Room to lie down with the load.
…You said set it down.
…Thought on it. Three days.
…Grandpa's load.
Asked on the road.
…Nobody knows.
From the very bottom of the load,
Tass draws out an old strap.
…Grandpa's strap.
From the day the load was lost.
…Knees ache.
Someday I can't carry it all.
…Before then, I trust one to you.
Hmm… want me to carry it?
Though bears only carry half.
Hands that never set anything down
…hold out a single strap.
I'll keep it. I won't open it.
…Yes.
That's how you keep a load.
…Big room.
Tonight I sleep beside the load.
…Not on top of it.
The lantern that flickered.
I saw it again tonight.
…It's still lit.
I've told no one.
Owls carry their promises
clutched in their talons.
The flickering one is the warm side.
Each time the wind blew,
the flame lay flat.
Selen's head turns without a sound
all the way to the window behind.
당신도 밤마다 창가에 서죠.\n바람 오는 쪽을 보면서.\n…하늘에서는 다:
You stand at the window nightly too,
facing where the wind comes from.
…From the sky, all is seen.
밤에도 배달해요? 대단해요!\n저는 밤엔 길을 잃어요.\n…낮에도 가끔:
You deliver at night? Amazing!
I get lost at night.
…By day too, sometimes.
I get lost by day.
…Between the two of us,
the whole day gets delivered.
Caught reading the wind.
By an owl.
그 등불까지 날 수 있어?: Can you fly to that lantern?
No letter needed.
Circling the lantern once
is news in itself.
…Understood.
Watching from afar is
a night messenger's work too.
I'll sleep when the sun is up.
Not facing the window today,
…but toward the warm side.
I flew to the warm-side lantern.
I circled it once,
…and the flame grew.
I only watched from afar.
The flicker has eased.
…Someone must have added wood.
Night messengers don't usually
tell their own stories, but.
From among the plumage, Selen
draws out an ash-grey feather.
Its tip is scorched.
할머니 깃털이에요.\n마녀사냥 때 사람들이\n'마녀 새'라며 불을 던졌대:
My grandmother's feather.
In the witch hunt, people
threw fire at the 'witch bird.'
Even so, Grandmother
delivered every last letter.
…To whom, I don't know.
Something flying over the roof.
Saw it three times.
…It was you.
No escaping a lynx's eyes.
…One more friend of the night.
An owl once called 'witch bird'
still carries letters to a witch.
I'll make you a perch on the roof.
지붕에요? 올빼미 자리요?: On the roof? An owl's perch?
…A night messenger with a roost —
first since my grandmother.
그 깃털, 창가에 걸까?: Hang the feather by the window?
…By the window.
It'll be seen from the sky.
Grandmother, beside the light.
I'll sleep when the sun is up.
Not afraid, this time.
…Under a lit roof.
…I'm back.
That's what one says to the pack.
…Changed the latch?
…I won't bite it this time.
Here. Witch's cat.
Two mice left.
The shutters were open.
…So I came.
Roof spot's free, right?
The four haven't come yet.
으음… 자리 잡으러 왔어.\n난로 옆, 비어 있지?:
Hmm… came to claim my spot.
By the stove's free, right?
Remembered a story about Grandpa.
…In my sleep.
Here again. Room for a nap?
…Just half a day.
I'm going east in spring!
…I'll pass on your regards!
토끼 안 드시죠?\n…알아요. 그냥 인사예요!:
You don't eat rabbits, right?
…I know. It's just a greeting!
I looked back before coming in!
…Nobody there. Phew.
Sent two guests toward the marsh.
Maps in hand. Heh heh.
Came by the shortcut.
…Truly quick this time.
Paid my respects to great-gran.
…Three tail swishes.
…The strap. Safe?
…Don't need to look. I know.
…Haven't set it down.
…Remember what you said, though.
I rested on the roof.
…I'll greet you after sundown.
Saw the window feather from the sky.
…So I didn't get lost.
The warm-side lantern is lit again.
That news first.
